purpose: Native evidence for the five forge.action.map.* rows the a-objective slice implements: the objective interaction channel (objective_state, objective_phase), the level's own exit win-condition item (extraction_enable) and the session checkpoint manager (checkpoint_save, checkpoint_restore). Members, signatures, RVA, slot and interop field offsets are the build 20403457 metadata; every claim about which machine executes a member is derived from the interop member kind and the state-replicator provider it belongs to, and nothing here was executed in game.
verification: Static only: interop metadata from the QA profile's Modules-ASM.dll and the decompiled wrappers under %TEMP%\covtrigb\ilspy\Modules\. No body was run and no runtime log was captured.
rules: Every IL2CPP interop body below is an il2cpp_runtime_invoke wrapper: the wrapper shows the signature, the slot and the parameter marshalling, never the native body. What the native body decides is therefore unproven from the managed side and is marked as such.

A member reachable only from a static entry in the interop assembly cannot be shown to replicate; the interaction channels (AttemptInteract on the objective manager, the checkpoint manager and the chained-puzzle instance) are the entries whose owning object is a state-replicator provider, and those are the ones this slice writes through.
`CallerCount` is the interop assembly's own count of managed call sites in the image. A zero is evidence that no managed caller exists, not that the member is dead.

stateShapes.notes: The struct carries no target status: a request cannot name the state to move to, only the interaction to ask for. The chain reaches the native side as ownerChainIndexPlusOne, a byte, so a chain index above 254 has no representation.
The payload is the interaction type plus the door lock position; there is no snapshot scope, no revision and no participant list in it.

stateVocabulary.notes: The status a request is asked for is not a field of the interaction payload; the objective's own machine derives it from the interaction it is given.
No zero member: the payload's default type is not a valid interaction.

members.name: AttemptInteract
members.entry: iSNet_StateReplicatorProvider interaction channel plus local-player paths (OnLocalPlayerFoundObjectiveItem, OnLocalPlayerEnterNewLayerType, OnExitScanProgressUpdate, UpdateFromInLevel)
members.sideBasis: state-replicator-provider (WardenObjectiveManager.GetStateReplicator) plus local callers; a client-local caller reaches the host through the same channel, which is what the replicated interaction is for

members.name: ForceCompleteObjectiveAll
members.sideBasis: static entry whose effect is published through the objective state replicator; the interop wrapper carries no authority check of its own, so the caller must be the host
members.notes: Names a layer and no chain: one call completes every chain that layer has, which is why the row's whole-layer form is this member and not the chain-addressed interaction.

members.name: ForceCompleteObjective
members.notes: Recorded but not reached: the two force entries differ only by name from the managed side, and the whole-layer member is the one whose behaviour the catalog's `CompleteChain` describes.

members.name: SetExtraTime
members.sideBasis: static entry on the objective manager, the same replication family as the interaction channel
members.notes: The dedicated extra-time entry: it names no layer and no chain, so the objective's own machine decides which timer the value belongs to. That is why the row's extra-time member reaches this member instead of the general interaction.

members.name: HasWardenObjectiveDataForLayer
members.notes: The existence check the whole-layer form is gated on.

members.name: TryGetWardenObjective
members.notes: The address check: a layer plus a chain index resolves only when the level really built that chain, which is what makes `objective-unknown-target` a native answer rather than a table of this layer's own.

members.name: Current
members.sideBasis: process-wide singleton, exactly as the game exposes it
members.notes: The instance AttemptInteract is called on. The interop assembly exposes a setter as well as a getter because the field is assignable, which is why a session that was torn down can be seen as absent rather than as a stale object.

members.name: AttemptInteract
members.entry: state-replicator provider interaction channel of CheckpointManager.m_stateReplicator
members.sideBasis: state-replicator-provider (CheckpointManager.GetStateReplicator) with a replicated interaction payload
members.notes: The store and the reload are the two members of this one payload type.

members.name: StoreCheckpoint
members.sideBasis: static entry on the checkpoint manager
members.notes: NOT reached by this slice: it is a static call past the replicator, and nothing in the managed image shows it going through the interaction channel. The interaction member is used instead, and this record exists so the alternative is visible.

members.name: ReloadCheckpoint
members.sideBasis: static entry on the checkpoint manager
members.notes: NOT reached by this slice, for the same reason as StoreCheckpoint.

members.name: IsReloadingCheckpoint
members.notes: The readback this slice deliberately does not use: a reload that is still running would answer true, and reporting that as a completed restore would be a claim the action cannot back. It is recorded here as the observation half of the sibling trigger rows.

members.name: ActivateWinCondition
members.entry: the level's own win-condition item; the body calls NavMarker.SetVisible (a verified direct edge) and tail-jumps into ChainedPuzzleInstance.AttemptInteract
members.sideBasis: level object registered as a win-condition item; the sibling trigger row's evidence already records this member as host-side
members.notes: The caller count is zero in the image and the member is still reachable: the level registers the landing as an iWardenObjectiveWinConditionItem and the win-condition machine calls it through that interface, which is what the slot name records. That is also why the row can arm an exit the level itself built and cannot invent one.

members.name: DeactivateWinCondition
members.kind: virtual, final (its own method-info token, no interface slot name)
members.notes: UNPROVEN: no managed caller exists in the image and the native body is not visible from the interop wrapper (the metadata token is populated, so a body exists, and its native size is not read here). The row reaches it for `enabled=false`, and the outcome it produces is left to the extraction observation rather than claimed by the action. This is the one member of the five rows whose effect is not established by a second call site or by an existing direct edge.

members.name: Current
members.sideBasis: process-wide singleton the level sets when it builds the exit
members.notes: The instance the extraction row calls its two members on. A level with no landing leaves it null, which the row refuses as `objective-unavailable` rather than inventing an exit.

members.name: m_puzzle
members.notes: The exit scan instance the landing was built with. Recorded because the extraction row's effect is that scan's state, which the sibling trigger row observes; the action itself never writes the field.

members.name: StopAmbientAlarm
members.notes: Recorded because the alarm module reaches it; not this slice's member.

unproven: Every host/client claim: no body was executed and no runtime log was captured. The side values rest on the state-replicator interface the owning object implements, on the interface slot a member occupies, and on the managed caller set.

Whether CheckpointManager.AttemptInteract forwards to StoreCheckpoint/ReloadCheckpoint or performs the store itself. The managed wrappers show only the two signatures and their caller counts; the native bodies are not visible. This is why the slice submits through the interaction member and records the static members as the alternative it does not use.

What ElevatorShaftLanding.DeactivateWinCondition does. It is a depublicized interface implementation with no managed caller, so its effect is unverified; the row still reaches it for `enabled=false` because it is the only member of the exit item that names that direction, and the action claims nothing beyond the call.

Whether AttemptInteract runs on a client and forwards to the host, or is refused there. The action's own authority gate refuses a non-host side before any native read, so the question does not change what this slice does; it does change what a plan can expect when a client-local step reaches the row.

Whether the objective's own machine derives eWardenObjectiveStatus from the interaction types the slice sends as believed. The status vocabulary and the interaction vocabulary are both registered, but no direct edge between an interaction type and a status value is visible from the managed side.

The exact member index `SetItemSolved` reads (pWardenObjectiveInteraction.itemIndexPlusOne, offset 3, a byte plus one) and whether it is the same index the item-solve family in objective_progress uses. The slice sends itemID (offset 16) as the item index, which is the field the struct declares as an int; the byte field is left at zero.
inGameVerificationPlan: Load a level with a two-layer objective chain, call forge.action.map.objective_state with state=DiscoverObjective, and read the objective state trigger: the status must move from NotDiscovered and the trigger must publish before or after the call in the same tick.
Call objective_phase with phase=CompleteChain on a fully built layer and confirm the whole chain completes in one call, and that no chain-addressed call was required.
Call extraction_enable with enabled=false on a level whose win condition is armed and confirm whether the exit scan stops; if it does not, the row's false direction must be refused instead of issued.

Call checkpoint_save with a real door lock position and confirm the checkpoint really stores (the checkpoint trigger publishes, and a reload restores from it), then call checkpoint_restore and observe whether the world epoch advances and whether level-enter fires again.
Watch for a second reload or a duplicate store after a client submits the same request, to establish whether the interaction channel really does the forwarding.
